note: [SF] events.csv 2018-08-12 Salesforce Transit Center; landmark models salesforce_tower (built 2013.24-2018.02; 326.1 m, 61 floors), salesforce_transit_center (2010.6-2018.61), fremont_181 (2018), millennium_tower (2009).

title: The 49ers Move South
text: July 17, 2014: the San Francisco 49ers open Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, 40 miles from the city in their name and next door to the offices of Silicon Valley. Candlestick Park is torn down the next year. The new stadium hosts the Super Bowl in 2016 and again in 2026.
note: [South Bay] landmarks_southbay.csv levis_stadium (2014); landmarks.csv candlestick_park_1971 (-2015). Super Bowl 50 (February 7, 2016) and Super Bowl LX (February 8, 2026): general knowledge / the cited Wikipedia page.

title: The Napa Earthquake
text: August 24, 2014, 3:20 a.m.: a magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes just south of Napa, the strongest in the Bay Area since 1989. One person is killed and about 200 are hurt. Old brick buildings downtown lose walls and cornices, and wineries lose thousands of barrels.
note: [North Bay] Downtown Napa buildings (Sanborn tracings 1901 / 1910, rolls). The view shakes at the earthquake (effect = quake); no building in the data ends with it. Magnitude, time, casualties: the cited Wikipedia page.

title: The Leaning Tower
text: In 2016 the owners of apartments in the 58-story Millennium Tower learn that it has sunk 16 inches into the soft fill beneath downtown and is tilting. Its foundation does not reach bedrock. Engineers spend years, and about $100 million, adding piles that do.
note: [SF] SF building Millennium Tower (301 Mission St, 2009) on the fill of Yerba Buena Cove (fill_zones.csv). Sinking and tilt disclosed 2016; perimeter pile upgrade finished 2023: the cited Wikipedia page.

title: Mission Bay
text: Mission Bay was once a real bay, filled in by 1910 for railroad yards. Since 1998 the yards have given way to a university medical campus, laboratories and apartments. Chase Center, the Golden State Warriors' basketball arena, opens here on September 6, 2019.
note: [SF] fill_zones.csv sf_mission_bay_north (1869-1890), sf_mission_bay_south (1884-1910); redevelopment_areas.csv mission_bay (cleared 1998-2008; UCSF groundbreaking 1999); landmark model chase_center (built 2017.05-2019.68); sf_buildings in Mission Bay: 421 before 2010, 584 before 2020.

title: The Tubbs Fire
text: October 9, 2017: on a night of violent dry wind, a wildfire races from the hills near Calistoga into the city of Santa Rosa. More than 1,300 homes burn in the Coffey Park neighborhood alone. Fires across the region that month kill 44 people.
note: [North Bay] Fire-only stop: events.csv 2017-10-09 North Bay Firestorm (5,600 structures, 22 dead; 44 killed across the region's October fires); data/manual/fires/destroyed_structures.csv tubbs_2017 = 5,656 (Coffey Park 1,432 structures, 1,355 dwellings), dated 2017-10-09; rebuilt footprints return 2018-2021 (after this stop).

title: Shelter in Place
text: March 17, 2020: as a new coronavirus spreads, seven Bay Area health departments jointly order residents to stay home, among the first such orders in the United States. Downtown offices empty out, and years later many are still far from full.
note: [SF] events.csv 2020-03-17 Shelter in Place (joint order by seven Bay Area health departments takes effect; among the first COVID-19 measures in the U.S.). Map shows the downtown towers; nothing on the map changes. Office vacancy afterward: general knowledge.

title: Lightning
text: August 16, 2020: a rare summer storm throws thousands of lightning bolts onto dry hills and starts hundreds of fires around the bay. In the Santa Cruz Mountains they merge, burn 1,490 buildings and sweep through Big Basin's ancient redwoods, most of which survive. For weeks the whole region breathes smoke.
note: [Coast] data/manual/fires: 1,490 structures destroyed in the CZU Lightning Complex (CAL FIRE damage inspections, decision 42): they burn on screen (time-extension DISASTERS 2020.625); rebuilds by permit. Lightning siege of August 16-17, 2020: the cited Wikipedia page.

title: ChatGPT
text: November 30, 2022: from a converted warehouse at 575 Florida Street in the Mission District, a research company called OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a program that answers questions in fluent sentences. A million people try it within five days. A new technology boom begins.
note: [SF] SF buildings of the block (575 Florida St / 1960 Bryant St, industrial buildings of the 1920s). OpenAI leased 575 Florida St in 2020 and joined it to 1960 Bryant St as its headquarters (SF Standard, July 11, 2023: sfstandard.com/2023/07/11/openais-secretive-san-francisco-offices-installing-nap-rooms-a-museum-for-staffers/); its earlier office was the Pioneer Building, 3180 18th St. Release on November 30, 2022; a million users in five days: the cited Wikipedia page. Checked 2026-11.

title: A Star on Earth
text: December 5, 2022: at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, 192 laser beams crush a pellet of hydrogen fuel the size of a peppercorn. For an instant it gives off more energy than the lasers put in, a first for fusion, the reaction that powers the sun.
note: [East Bay] industrial_sites llnl; region building National Ignition Facility (named in the Overture data). Ignition shot of December 5, 2022 (2.05 MJ in, 3.15 MJ out): general knowledge / the cited Wikipedia page.

title: The Chips Behind AI
text: Nvidia, founded in 1993 to make graphics chips for video games, turns out to make the best chips for training artificial intelligence, and orders flood in. In 2023 the Santa Clara company is valued at $1 trillion; by October 2025, at $5 trillion, more than any company before it.
note: [South Bay] Region buildings NVIDIA Endeavor (2017) and NVIDIA Voyager (2022), named in the Overture data. $1 trillion in mid-2023, first $5 trillion company on October 29, 2025 (checked 2026-11: Reuters reports of that day): the cited Wikipedia page.

title: Cars Without Drivers
text: June 25, 2024: Waymo, a company that grew out of Google, opens its driverless taxi service to anyone in San Francisco, after years of testing on the city's streets. White cars with spinning sensors on the roof and nobody at the wheel become an everyday sight.
note: [SF] The map shows downtown streets with generic moving cars (procedural traffic, decision 15), not Waymo vehicles. Open to all riders in San Francisco on June 25, 2024 (checked 2026-11: Axios, June 25, 2024): the cited Wikipedia page.

title: Oakland Loses Its Teams
text: For decades three major-league teams share this one site in Oakland. Basketball's Warriors, champions here in 2015, move to San Francisco in 2019, and football's Raiders leave for Las Vegas in 2020. On September 26, 2024, baseball's A's play their last game at the Coliseum.
note: [East Bay] landmarks_eastbay.csv oakland_coliseum (1966 / 1996 rebuild) and oakland_arena (1966). Warriors' 2015 title and 2019 move, Raiders' move (2020), A's final game on September 26, 2024: general knowledge / the cited Wikipedia page.

title: The AI Boom
text: The new AI companies cluster in San Francisco. OpenAI takes half a million square feet of offices in Mission Bay; Anthropic fills buildings along Howard Street. Downtown, emptied by the pandemic, begins to fill again, and in 2025 rents here rise faster than in any other big American city.
note: [SF] SF downtown and South of Market towers (500 Howard St among them). Checked 2026-11: OpenAI's 486,600 sq ft sublease at 1455 and 1515 Third St, October 2023 (The Real Deal); Anthropic at 500 Howard St from 2023, over 900,000 sq ft on Howard St by 2026 (CoStar, Bisnow); AI firms the largest share of new office leasing (CBRE via the cited article); San Francisco first among large U.S. cities in rent growth in 2025 (Apartment List, +11.5 % in the year to August 2025; missionlocal.org/2025/09/sf-evictions-rents-rising-ai-boom/). Whether AI alone explains the rents is disputed.

title: The Bay Area Today
text: Two and a half centuries after a Spanish scouting party first saw the bay, 7.8 million people live in the nine counties around it. The shoreline is largely man-made, but the bay is no longer being filled: old salt ponds are being returned to the tides.
note: [Region] population.csv bay_area_9county 2020 = 7,765,640; fill_zones.csv (303 dated zones; restored rows sm_bair_island_restored 1983-2015, nb_napa_ponds_restored 2006-15, sb_island_ponds_restored 2006); map extent = ten counties (decision 32).
